patch.description: Replace all editable values of the submitted existing items in one transaction. Send only changed rows, each once, with its original expected_revision and an explicit values array. The expected_configuration_revision must match the field configuration used for the draft. Configuration, missing-item, ownership, value-validation, revision, or storage failures roll back the complete batch, including revisions, timestamps and value tombstones. Automatic IDs remain unchanged and omitted editable values are tombstoned. Successful replacements advance each submitted item revision once, including no-op replacements, without changing the inventory configuration revision. The response contains saved items in request order. Preserve failed drafts and explicitly discard/reload after conflicts; never automatically retry stale revisions.

200.description: Every submitted replacement committed successfully, returned in request order.

404.description: Inventory or submitted item is missing, deleted, or belongs to another inventory. No changes were saved.

409.description: An item revision is stale/exhausted or the inventory configuration changed. No changes were saved. Row conflicts include detail.item_id.

422.description: Malformed or duplicate rows, invalid revisions, or invalid field values. No changes were saved. Domain value errors include detail.item_id; schema errors include the items array index in loc.

patch.description: Apply inventory metadata, field operations, and option operations in one transaction. Any validation, ownership, or storage failure rolls back all changes. Omitted operation arrays leave existing records unchanged. Existing field types and text limits cannot be changed; group membership is preserved. Each existing field or option may be changed only once per save, and options cannot be changed when their field is being deleted. New fields include their initial options in their create data. Deleting a field clears its stored values and options while retaining deletion tombstones. Field order is optional and must reference the complete final field set. New ID fields backfill existing active items in this transaction; any later failure rolls back those assignments too. The required expected_revision must match the snapshot loaded through GET configuration. Every accepted draft advances the revision, including no-op saves; field, option, and metadata writes may advance it further. The response contains the final revision. Concurrent configuration changes, including changes through individual endpoints or group membership changes, cause HTTP 409 without applying any draft changes. Item value changes and automatic ID counter increments do not invalidate configuration snapshots. Clients must preserve the draft and request an explicit discard-and-reload instead of automatically retrying.

post.summary: Stage a managed file for an attachment field
post.description: Stream a binary file as application/octet-stream. X-File-Name is required and must contain encodeURIComponent-style URI-encoded UTF-8. Optional X-File-Type stores the declared MIME type; it is not trusted for inline rendering. The application imposes no per-file size limit; uploads are streamed to disk. Uploads do not change item/configuration revisions. Save the returned ID through the ordinary item create/PATCH or atomic batch endpoint to claim it; unclaimed uploads expire after 24 hours through maintenance.

post.summary: Prepare a complete inventory ZIP export
post.description: Creates a version-1 ZIP containing inventory.json and all referenced managed originals. Files stream to private scratch storage and are verified against saved sizes/SHA-256. Rejects source changes during preparation. Returns only after completion; the opaque single-use download token expires after 15 minutes. No inventory or item data/revisions are changed. Client disconnection cancels preparation.

post.summary: Validate an inventory archive and stage an import preview
post.description: Streams ZIP/ZIP64 into private staging and validates layout, typed manifest, file sizes, CRC and SHA-256 without creating database records. No attachment or ZIP byte-size cap. Metadata processing bounds: 64 MiB JSON and 524,290 entries. Rejects encrypted/nonregular/unsafe/extra/missing/duplicate entries and unsupported compression; accepts Store/Deflate. Preview expires after 30 minutes. Disconnect cancels copying/validation.

post.summary: Atomically create an independent inventory from a validated preview
post.description: Optional metadata overrides preserve absent archived name/description. Uses fresh technical identities, preserved automatic numbers/counters, order and historical saved-state semantics. Rechecks/copies staged files then publishes one SQLite transaction. Identical concurrent/repeated requests return one inventory; changed retry parameters return 409. Confirmation continues after disconnect and receipts remain recoverable for 30 minutes. No existing inventory is overwritten.

value.title: Value
value.description: Value matching the field type. URL fields use InventoryUrlValue. Duration uses non-negative integer seconds up to 9007199254740991. Required fields must be supplied when creating or replacing an item. Never submit ID field values; the server generates them and preserves them during complete replacement. Checkbox values must be true or false, never strings or numbers. Table toggles submit a complete replacement of editable values and must satisfy all current required fields. Attachment values are non-empty arrays of unique staged or same-item attachment IDs scoped to this inventory and field. Omit an optional attachment field to remove all its files; an empty array is invalid. IDs owned by other items or fields are rejected. Claims and removals participate in the same item/batch transaction.
